title: ChronoMap: request pathway inspector for deep trace exploration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Engineers need a faster way to understand causal relationships across spans when investigating multi-hop inference requests (e.g., frontend -> router -> shard -> runtime). Current waterfall and span lists are valuable but require too much context switching and manual correlation across panes.

Goal: Design a companion view — ChronoMap — that surfaces the full request pathway as an interactive, zoomable lane map with span grouping, correlation ID overlays, and contextual filters. The intent is to reduce mean time to root cause (MTTR) for request-level incidents and make tracing approachable for product engineers.

Scope: This ticket covers low-fidelity -> mid-fidelity prototypes, a short usability review with 3 platform engineers, and design specs for handoff (Figma + annotated component checklist). Does not include instrumentation or backend schema changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates: timeline zoom, lane grouping (runtime, network, storage), pinned correlation breadcrumbs, request-level annotations (cache hits, fallback events), and span highlighting on hover.
- UX flows: drill from ChronoMap to span detail panel, persist filters across navigation, and shareable deep-link to a timestamped view.
- Designer sign-off and engineering review with feasibility notes and list of required telemetry fields.
comments: 2026-02-17 | Priya Kaur (PM): Great framing. Please ensure we surface model-variant and region labels on the lane map so ops can triage region-specific regressions.

2026-02-19 | Diego Ramirez (Design): Added two variants of zoom: time-ruler linear and focus+context fisheye. Fisheye helps surface short-lived spans without losing macro view. Shared Figma v1: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/chrono-map-v1

2026-02-21 | Liam O'Connor (Engine): We can't add model-variant to every span without a backend index change. Can we start by showing variant when present in span metadata and flag spans with missing metadata?

2026-02-24 | Ava Chen (Design): Updated prototype to include sparse-variant badges and soft placeholders for missing fields. Added a lightweight correlation-id explorer (typeahead) tied to the map. Prototype link: https://airtable-proto.redwood/chrono/preview
2026-02-26 | Maya Singh (SRE): Suggest adding an explicit 'fallback event' glyph for model downgrade fallbacks so we can quickly filter regressions caused by automatic fallback policies.

2026-03-01 | Diego Ramirez (Design): Collected usability notes from 3 engineers. Key findings: (1) lane stacking by component (router, shard, runtime) was preferred over chronological lane per service; (2) users want a persisted filter bar; (3) deep-linking to a span + scrub position essential for postmortems. Updated design spec and next steps below.
decision: Proceed with lane-grouping by functional responsibility (router / shard / runtime / infra). Implement a hybrid zoom model (linear time + fisheye focus). Surface model-variant and region where available; show a 'metadata missing' affordance otherwise. Use a distinct glyph (hollow diamond) for fallback events. Deep-links encoded as /trace/<trace_id>?t=<ms>&lane=<lane>&focus=<span_id>.
next_steps: Finalize mid-fi Figma and annotate component token variants (colors, glyphs, density rules)
Create engineering RFC describing required telemetry fields (model_variant, region, fallback_flag, cache_hit) and expected sample rates
Run 2 short usability sessions with infra and product engineers focused on failure triage flows
Create a stubbed console route for deep-link tests and pass through existing trace data for end-to-end validation
